title: Human Forensic Biobanks: A Scoping Review Protocol
content: Human forensic biobanks preserve biological materials and associated information for forensic investigation, evidence retention, research, quality assurance, method development, and training, yet the terminology, purposes, governance, and operating models of these resources remain heterogeneous across forensic disciplines. This scoping review will map how human forensic biobanks and related forensic imaging or data repositories are defined, established, operated, governed, and used. The review will follow the Arksey and O’Malley framework with refinements by Levac and colleagues and will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Embase will be searched without date, geographic, or search-language restrictions, supplemented by reference-list and forward-citation searching. Eligible evidence will describe established human biological collections, retained biological evidence repositories, or qualifying forensic digital repositories with documented forensic purposes. Two reviewers will independently screen records; data will be charted using a piloted form and verified by a second reviewer. Findings will be synthesized descriptively and narratively, with publications distinguished from unique resources and physical, digital, and hybrid models mapped separately. The review is expected to characterize resource purposes, populations, specimens, and data types, governance, access, quality management, sustainability, and reported applications, while identifying implementation challenges and reporting gaps. By organizing a fragmented literature around the underlying resources rather than individual analytical findings, the review will provide a structured evidence base for future forensic biobank development, governance, and research.
